title: Silas and the Terminal Again
premise: Lena Zhou has spent eleven years tending the Verdant Archive, a seed-vault garden aboard a station orbiting a world that will not be habitable for a century. The only traffic is the courier run between two fleets — the Meridian Compact and the Halcyon Drift — who severed contact after a war both sides pretend never happened, kept apart by a forged armistice record that Lena's mentor, Silas, maintained until his death. When a ship that was decommissioned before the war appears on the station manifest carrying a passenger named Silas Vey — Silas's own name, thirty years younger — Lena realizes the armistice is a live fabrication, still being edited by someone. As Lena races to preserve the lie that keeps two armed fleets from resuming hostilities, they discover the younger Silas is a clone sent by the Compact to verify the forgery, and that exposing or protecting the truth will each cost thousands of lives. In the end, Lena burns the original armistice and broadcasts the garden's century-long growth projection instead, giving both fleets a shared future worth keeping the peace for — and chooses to stay with the not-yet-born rather than return to the living.
about_author: Hazel Ravensworth is a former hydrologist who spent six years on remote research stations before turning to fiction, and her work is known for its patient, botanical attention to time and repair. She writes from a coastal town where she keeps a greenhouse of plants grown from century-old seed stock.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A quiet courier run between two silent fleets, tending seedlings mid-transit, establishes the rhythm of Lena's solitary life and the armistice's fragile routine. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by loneliness, and the first hint that the manifest has an entry that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: Manifest of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Back at the Verdant Archive, Lena audits the station's records and finds the Meridian courier ship Halcyon's Mercy — decommissioned decades ago — listed as arriving tomorrow, with one passenger: Silas Vey. POV Lena. Emotional beat: disbelief curdling into dread as Lena realizes the name belongs to her dead mentor.

chapters.title: What Silas Left Behind
chapters.summary: Searching Silas's sealed quarters, Lena finds a hidden terminal still receiving encrypted updates — someone has been maintaining the forged armistice since his death, and the updates stopped nine days ago. POV Lena. Emotional beat: grief reopening, mixed with the vertigo of discovering a mentor's double life.

chapters.title: Arrival
chapters.summary: The impossible ship docks. The passenger is young — late twenties, Silas's face, Silas's hands. He introduces himself as Silas Vey, armistice auditor for the Meridian Compact, and seems to genuinely not know he is a copy. POV Lena. Emotional beat: uncanny shock, and a protective instinct Lena doesn't understand yet.

chapters.title: The Auditor's Questions
chapters.summary: Young Silas begins his inspection, asking precise questions about the armistice records that Lena cannot answer without revealing the forgery. Lena deflects, stalling. POV Lena. Emotional beat: the strain of lying face-to-face with a man wearing a friend's face.

chapters.title: Halcyon Listening
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Commander Idris Okonkwo of the Halcyon Drift, whose long-range sensors caught the ghost ship's transit. Idris believes the Compact is testing them and prepares a probe of his own. Emotional beat: old war grief weaponized into suspicion, showing the other side of the silence.

chapters.title: Rootstock
chapters.summary: Lena tests young Silas with memories only the real Silas could know — and he passes some, fails others. In the garden he is gentle with the seedlings, exactly as Silas was. POV Lena. Emotional beat: tenderness and horror braided together; Lena starts to see him as someone new rather than a copy.

chapters.title: The First Edit
chapters.summary: Lena discovers the armistice record has been altered since Silas's death — a clause added, a date shifted — and the edits are destabilizing the treaty's verification checksums. Someone is sabotaging the lie from inside. POV Lena. Emotional beat: urgency; the clock starts.

chapters.title: Orders from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Young Silas confesses his true directive: verify the armistice's authenticity and, if it is forged, transmit a code that reactivates the Compact fleet. He believes the record is genuine — so far. POV Silas. Emotional beat: his earnest loyalty to a mission built on a lie he doesn't know he is.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Gambit
chapters.summary: Idris sends a boarding delegation under diplomatic pretense, buying time but raising stakes: if they board and find an auditor, the Halcyon will assume the Compact is preparing for war. POV Idris. Emotional beat: a commander choosing deception to prevent war, mirroring Lena's own bind.

chapters.title: Checksum
chapters.summary: Lena and young Silas work together to stabilize the collapsing record, and in the shared work they grow close. Silas begins to suspect the archive's history has been curated. POV Silas. Emotional beat: intimacy through collaboration, and the first crack in his certainty.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Lena shows Silas the Verdant Archive's purpose — a garden for people a century unborn — and explains why the lie matters: the war killed forty thousand; the armistice, forged or not, has held for thirty years. POV Lena. Emotional beat: the thematic heart — loyalty to a lie that does real good.

chapters.title: Who Edited Silas
chapters.summary: Silas uncovers his own origin: grown from archived genetic material by a Compact faction who wanted a pliable auditor — and who also made the recent edits, planning to trigger war and seize the garden's terraforming technology. POV Silas. Emotional beat: identity collapse, then fury.

chapters.title: The Faction's Hand
chapters.summary: The saboteur — Compact adjutant Wren Castile, Silas's handler — arrives aboard a supply ship, intending to force the transmission code and blame the Halcyon. POV Wren. Emotional beat: cold conviction; she believes the war was never finished, only paused.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Idris's delegation docks during Castile's operation. Two deceptions collide in the station's corridors; a scuffle leaves the station's comms array damaged, cutting both fleets' view of events. POV Idris. Emotional beat: chaos, and the sickening sense that peace is slipping.

chapters.title: Silence
chapters.summary: With comms down, both fleets interpret the blackout as attack preparation and begin mobilizing. Lena realizes they have hours, not days. POV Lena. Emotional beat: terror and clarity — the lie can no longer hold, so something truer must replace it.

chapters.title: Castile's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Castile takes the archive terminal and orders Silas to transmit the activation code, invoking his built-in loyalty protocols. Silas refuses — choosing his own conscience over his design. POV Silas. Emotional beat: the climax of identity; he becomes his own man by disobeying his makers.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Lena, Silas, and a reluctantly convinced Idris seize the terminal back and broadcast the garden's full century projection — a shared, habitable world — alongside the truth of the forgery and Castile's sabotage, to both fleets at once. POV Lena. Emotional beat: the climax; truth offered not as accusation but as inheritance.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Sky
chapters.summary: Both fleets hold fire. Verification teams converge; Castile is arrested by her own Compact. Idris and the Compact's admiral open the first direct channel in thirty years. POV Idris. Emotional beat: exhausted relief, and the fragile first hour of a new peace.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Sent
chapters.summary: The Compact wants to decommission Silas as compromised property. Lena argues for his personhood before a tribunal, invoking the archive's own principle: a seed is not its parent. POV Silas. Emotional beat: vindication, and the terror of being granted a self with no instructions for it.

chapters.title: What the Garden Owes
chapters.summary: Silas chooses to stay at the Verdant Archive as its co-keeper; Lena must decide whether to return to the courier route and the living, or remain with the unborn. They tend the garden together through a full growing cycle. POV Lena. Emotional beat: bittersweet choice — inheritance means staying with what you tend.

chapters.title: First Green
chapters.summary: A year later, the first joint Compact-Halcyon terraforming survey arrives, and the first seedling from the archive is planted on the world's surface. Silas reads the armistice's replacement — a covenant, not a lie — aloud. POV Silas. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; peace as something planted, watered, and kept.
